messages:
Maria Gonzales: Heads-up — HyperCart is asking for a Dedicated commit in eu-west with burst. They want guidance on a safe buffer and pricing options. They run a mix of chat + embeddings, mostly small sequences. Can infra & sales give a quick recommendation?

Lee Park: Quick Q — what model family and 95th pct sequence length? that drives GPU-hours. Also are they okay with cross-region fallback for overflow?

Maria Gonzales: Model mix: 70% open-chat (approx 2k tokens avg/session), 30% embeddings (short). 95th pct seq ~ 3k tokens. They asked for baseline commit that covers 99th pct day. Region constraint: EU data residency for latencies — fallback allowed only for anonymized requests.

Sanjay Patel: Did a rough forecast from their q1 telemetry. If we assume 1.2M prompt+response tokens/day at 3k seq, that's ~400 sessions/day. Using our perf numbers (A100-ish equiv) -> ~480 GPU-hours/day. Rough calc: ```tokens_per_day = 1.2e6
sessions = tokens_per_day / 3000 ~ 400
avg_gpu_sec_per_session ~ 4320s -> gpu_hours = sessions * 4320 / 3600 ~ 480``` So baseline commit = 20 GPUs * 24h = 480 GPU-hours.

Lee Park: Nice. For safety I'd add a warm-pool + live batching headroom. Operationally I prefer commit = 20 GPUs + buffer. Proposal: buffer 15-25% depending on SLA. 20% is a good starter.

Chris O'Neill: Operational constraints in eu-west: our on-hand A100 pool is ~92% utilized in peak windows. If we take 20% buffer that's tight without prewarming. Suggest we do: commit 20 GPUs + 4 GPU buffer (20%), plus 6 GPUs warm-pool (prewarmed with KV caches for top prompts) to shave cold-starts. Warm pool can be ephemeral and billed at lower rate when idle.

Kai Liu: Note cross-region fallback = extra egress + peering costs. If we route anonymized overflow to us-west, add ~0.5-0.8ms p99 extra latency (network) plus egress cost. For embeddings heavy flows avoid fallback. We should tag requests as fallback-eligible in policy.

Sales-Amy: From pricing side we can offer two options: (A) 15% burst credit at +20% price premium, non-guaranteed; (B) 25% guaranteed burst at +50% premium with SLA-backed priority. If they want guaranteed headroom during campaigns, we should push B. Also can trade a longer commit term for lower premium.

Maria Gonzales: Ops question — how do we enforce the buffer so it doesn't blow cost during surge? Can we implement automatic shed policy + fallback to cheaper quantized model?

Chris O'Neill: Yes — policy layers: 1) shed best-effort non-critical requests, 2) fallback to quantized model variants (lower tokens/sec cost), 3) enable cross-region if allowed. We'll add per-route cost thresholds and token-based throttles.

Sanjay Patel: Running cost estimate for proposed commit: commit = 24 GPUs total (20 baseline + 4 buffer). 24 * 24h = 576 GPU-hours/day. With expected avg util 85% effective -> ~490 effective GPU-hours/day matches demand. Burst window: allow additional 12 GPUs for up to 48 hours at +50% premium in option B.

ops-bot: [automated] eu-west GPU util (7d avg): 92% peak, queued jobs +8% this week. No maintenance windows scheduled.

Maria Gonzales: Summary / action items: - Recommend offering HyperCart commit = 20 GPUs baseline + 4 GPU buffer (20%). - Sales to present pricing Option B (48h 12-GPU guaranteed burst @ +50%) and Option A (15% non-guaranteed @ +20%). - Infra to run warm-pool experiment (preload KV caches for top-5 prompts) next week and measure cold-start delta. - Add fallback tagging for anonymized requests + egress cost calc. We will canary the config on Tue. :thumbsup:
